transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I've been dealing with some really awful, unwanted thoughts recently. I'm an artist, and I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt... and I just kept getting these thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. 

It was like, if I made one wrong photo placement or chose the wrong color, it meant I didn't love her enough. I usually get normal creative doubts with my work, but I couldn't just brush these off like I usually do. It really started to get to me, so I figured I should talk to someone about it.

When you have these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking your work over and over, redoing parts of it, or seeking reassurance from others—to try to make the anxious feeling go away?

Yeah, I do. Um, I'll end up rereading the label text I wrote, or just... nudging the same objects around on my work table. I'll check the layout photos over and over again until it finally feels 'settled' to me. It's frustrating because part of me knows it's already fine, and I know I'm just losing studio time by doing all that, but it feels like I have to do it to make the feeling go away.

Do you notice this kind of intrusive doubt-and-checking pattern happening with other tasks or projects in your life, or has it really only shown up around this particular memorial piece for your aunt?

No, honestly, I think it's really just been with this memorial piece. I mean, I always have a little bit of regular perfectionism when I'm working on a commission or something, but nothing like this. I haven't noticed myself getting stuck in that kind of checking loop with my other art, or really with anything else in my life. It seems like it's just tied to this specific project for my aunt.
Can you tell me when your aunt passed away, and how soon after that these intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors started?

Um, to be honest, I'm not exactly sure on the timeline. I don't really have the specific date she passed away right in my head at the moment... it's all been a bit of a blur recently. And as for the thoughts and the checking, I didn't really notice a specific day when that started, either. It just sort of... crept up on me gradually while I was in the middle of working on the piece.

Since your aunt passed away, have you also been feeling persistently sad, tearful, or down, or noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, or interest in things beyond just the worries about this art piece?

No, not really. I mean, obviously I was sad when she passed, but... I haven't been feeling persistently down or tearful or anything like that lately. My sleep and appetite are pretty normal. And I'm still interested in my other art and my regular life. It really is just the stress and the worry around getting this one memorial piece right.
Roughly how many weeks or months has it been since you first started noticing these intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors around the memorial piece?

I'm really not sure, to be honest. I don't have a good sense of exactly how many weeks or months it's been. Like I said, it kind of just crept up on me while I was working on it, so I don't have a clear timeline of when it all started.
On a typical day, roughly how many hours would you estimate you spend caught up in these thoughts or doing the checking and rearranging behaviors?

Um... I haven't really timed it, so I don't have an exact number for you. It's hard to say how many hours it actually adds up to. It mostly just happens in bursts when I'm in the studio working on the piece. I'll get stuck checking and rearranging things for a bit, but... yeah, I'm really not sure what the total time would be on a typical day.

When you have these worries about the piece being wrong, is the core fear really about disappointing or dishonoring your aunt specifically, or is it more a general fear that you made a mistake or something bad will happen if it's not perfect, regardless of who the piece is for?

Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't thought about it quite like that. I guess I don't really know if it's specifically about her, or if it's just a general fear of making a mistake. It all just sort of blends together when I'm working on it, so I couldn't really tell you which one it is at its core. I just know it feels wrong if I don't get it right.
Can you tell me approximately how long ago your aunt passed away — for example, was it within the last few weeks, a couple of months, or longer than three months ago?

Um... I don't really remember exactly. I'm sorry, I just... I don't have a good grasp on the timeline of when she passed. It's all a bit of a blur, so I couldn't tell you if it was a few weeks or a few months ago.

Aside from the worry about honoring your aunt, do you ever get that same 'it has to feel just right' feeling or urge to redo/rearrange things in other parts of your life that have nothing to do with her or her memory?

No, I don't think so. It's really just... well, mostly just when I'm working on my art. I haven't really noticed having to redo things or needing them to feel perfectly right in other parts of my day-to-day life. It seems to just happen when I'm in the studio.
Before your aunt passed away, had you ever experienced this kind of intrusive doubt-and-checking pattern with any of your art projects, even briefly?

Um, no, I don't think I did. I mean, I've always wanted my pieces to turn out well, but... I don't remember ever getting stuck like this before she passed. I never really had that constant doubting or feeling like I needed to check things over and over back then. It really just seems to have started recently.
Beyond the extra time it's taking in the studio, has this worry affected other parts of your life — like meeting deadlines, your relationships, or your ability to focus on daily responsibilities?

Well, for the most part, I'm still getting my daily stuff done. But... the extra time I lose in the studio is definitely catching up with me. It actually cost me a grant deadline recently. And I even had to back out of a gallery talk that I really wanted to do, just because I was so behind. So, yeah, it has affected things a bit.

When you're in the studio working on this piece, does this checking and doubting happen almost every single session, and has that been going on continuously for several weeks now, or has it only come up a couple of times?

Um, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't exactly kept track of how many weeks it's been going on or... or if it happens every single time I go in there. I know it's been an issue recently, but I couldn't tell you for certain if it's a continuous, every-session kind of thing or just... something that happens some of the time.

When you're caught up in checking and rearranging, are you specifically picturing your aunt or worrying about her memory in that moment, or does it feel more like a general 'this isn't right yet' sensation that isn't really about her?

It's definitely about her. Um, when I'm working on it, I keep getting these... these awful, unwanted thoughts that I'm going to dishonor her somehow. It's not just a general feeling of it not being right. It's more like, if I make one wrong photo placement or choose the wrong color, it means I didn't love her enough. And I just can't seem to brush those thoughts off like my normal creative doubts.
